newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas futures lose more ground late.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas futures lose more ground late.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures continued to lose ground late Monday in lackluster trader, hit by more technical selling and forecasts for milder East Coast weather that undermined the cash, industry sources said.
At 1410 EST, December skidded 6.2 cents to $2.60 per million British thermal units, while January was 6.4 cents lower at $2.58. Other deferreds were off by two to 5.7 cents.

"Short-term, the weather is helping us ease a bit, but I'd be careful about being too bearish at this stage," said one Midwest trader, noting volume has been light on down days and sentiment could quickly change with colder weather.
Traders said forecasts for milder East Coast temperatures this week helped pressure the physical market early Monday. But few doubted prices would quickly rebound with the next cold snap.

Technically, some chartists pegged near-support in December at $2.57 and then in the $2.52 area. Most agreed a close below $2.62 should trigger more selling near-term. Resistance was seen at Friday's high of $2.72, then at the $2.88 contract high and then at $2.92 and $2.98, prominent spot continuation chart highs set in late June and early July.

Cash sources said Gulf Coast prices were down about five cents Monday to about the $2.70 area. Midwest prices slipped almost a dime to the mid-$2.50s. New York city gate swing gas was quoted in the $3.05-3.10 area, off more than 15 cents.
NYMEX said 19,379 Hub contracts traded at 1340 EST.
NYMEX December Canadian natgas was still off by one-half cent at $1.23, while deferreds were untraded at 1400 EST. NYMEX said 29 Alberta contracts traded at 1340 EST.
NYMEX Permian natgas remained untraded at 1400 EST, but December was still offered one cent lower at $2.53.
On the KCBT, December tumbled seven cents to $2.49, while deferreds were unchanged to two cents lower. The December East/West spread widened by 0.8 cent to 11 cents (NYMEX premium).
